prompt: A polling firm estimates the share of adults in a county who stream TV by calling randomly chosen LANDLINE numbers on weekday afternoons. Which source of bias is the most serious concern?

choices.label: Response bias from callers lying about streaming
Undercoverage: adults without landlines, and those at work, cannot be reached
Voluntary response, because people chose to pick up the phone
There is no bias, because the numbers were chosen randomly

hint: Random selection only helps if everyone in the population has a chance to be selected. Who has NO chance here?

hints.text: Random selection only helps if everyone in the population has a chance to be selected. Who has NO chance here?
Younger adults and renters often have no landline, and most working adults are not home on weekday afternoons. Those groups probably stream more.
Whole groups are left out of the sampling frame: undercoverage, choice B.

explanation: The sampling frame is landline numbers answered on weekday afternoons. Cell-only households and people at work are missing from it entirely.
Those missing groups likely stream more than retirees at home with a landline, so the estimate will be too low.
Systematically leaving out part of the population is undercoverage. Choice B. Random dialing within a bad frame does not fix it, so D is wrong.

alternativeExplanations.title: Frame vs population
steps: Population: all adults in the county. Frame: the list you actually draw from, here landline numbers.
When the frame is smaller than the population in a lopsided way, you get undercoverage.
A better design would include cell numbers and call at varied times.
